title: Check the request before the generator
statement: When a request contradicts itself or the course's scope, or different generators fail it the same way, fix or reject the request before changing the generator.
example: In one gap analysis, 2 of 4 wrong-unit failures were faults in the benchmark's own data.
detail: In the AP generator's benchmark, two different models hard-failed the same document-based item, which the notes take as a sign that some evaluation samples are intrinsically difficult: a wrong unit mapping, an impossible spec, or a judge edge case (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/data/model_findings.md`). On one topic the judge failed one item for leaving out a civilization its objective named and another for including it, as belonging to a different course, and it failed an item whose request labelled a document-based essay easy, a level it ruled such a task can't have (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/python/benchmark_results/unit_1/diagnosis.md`). In the final gap analysis, 2 of 4 wrong-unit failures were benchmark data quality issues (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/python/CLAUDE.md`).
against: Whether a task type can be easy is the judge's view, and a scaffolded short source task could be easy for some students. That a request was impossible is inferred from two models failing the same item, and the notes themselves list other explanations, among them a judge edge case (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/data/model_findings.md`).

evidence.quote: Both models hard-failed at the same DBQ item (item 33) — confirming some eval samples are intrinsically difficult (wrong unit mapping, impossible spec, or IB v2.4.0 edge case).
The question fails to address the specific learning objective requested (Inca Empire) and instead focuses on a different group (Pueblo peoples).
The question targets the wrong curriculum. AP US History focuses on societies in what is now the United States; the Inca Empire is a South American civilization assessed in AP World History.
There is a clear mismatch between the labeled difficulty ('easy') and the actual task complexity.
- **4 curriculum alignment** (wrong unit) -- 2 are benchmark data quality issues (unfixable)
